newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: New freight handling operation at Rottderam.
newsitem.headline: New freight handling operation at Rottderam.

text.p: A new airfreight handling facility has been opened at Rotterdam airport by the Dutch transport group Racon and the airport operating company, Rotterdam Airport BV, Racon director Leen Lok said.
He told Reuters in a telephone interview the new facility will provide competition for two existing companies at the airport, Servisair and Avia Presto, part of the Royal Pakhoed group of companies.

Racon, part of the independently-owned Dutch Transport Manangement International group owned by Dutch transport sector entrepreneur Wibo Aris, has occupied a 7,000 sq. metre warehouse built by the airport operating company Rotterdam Airport BV at a cost of 2.5 million guilders.

The company is marketing a pallet consolidating and deconsolidating service to shippers. This is expected to be used by Dutch fruit exporters, who truck produce to Rotterdam airport to have it palletised before it is ferried to a number of other airfreight centres, including Schiphol airport.
Rotterdam's own runway is too short for large freighter-based export operators, industry sources said.
Lok added that he also is hopeful of developing new business at the airport using Racon's connections in the textiles business.

He said in the first part of next year, Racon will move into a new 1000 square m. facility currently being built by the airport operating company. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 8982 Fax +44 171 542 5017
